ingredients.item: Salmon fillets, skin on or off

instructions: Put the Dijon, honey, vinegar, vegetable oil, minced garlic, salt and pepper in a jar. Close the lid and shake for 30 seconds, until it's smooth and thick. That should be about 3/4 cup.
Pat the salmon dry with paper towels. Put the fillets in a bowl, add 1/4 cup of the glaze and turn them to coat. They don't need to sit.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the salmon, skin side down if it has skin, and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, until the underside is deep golden.

Flip the salmon and cook for 3 to 4 minutes. You're cooking it to 145°F at the thickest part, so if you have a thermometer, check it there. No thermometer? Press the thickest part with a fork: it's done when it flakes.
Stir the whole grain mustard into the remaining glaze. Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Divide the arugula among 4 plates. Serve the salmon on the arugula with the sauce spooned over the top.
method_notes: Spend With Pennies (5.0 from 31) leads: a shaken honey, Dijon and vinegar glaze, a quick toss with no marinating, a medium skillet, and the rest of the glaze stirred with whole grain mustard as a sauce. The lead's glaze (1 cup) is cut to about 3/4 cup, still plenty for coating and a sauce. A Sassy Spoon (4.6 from 42) brushes the glaze on in the last minute and serves over arugula, so the arugula comes from there. All ingredients are naturally gluten-free, dairy-free and nut-free (check the mustard labels).
